exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean birth vs vaginal birth)
outcome: Coverage of maternal and newborn health-care interventions
cohort: 23,471 women and their newborn babies admitted to five hospitals in Bangladesh, Nepal, and Tanzania
finding: Exit surveys and hospital register data had low accuracy for assessing coverage of specific clinical interventions around the time of birth, except for self-report of KMC, which had high sensitivity.
mod_finding: Caesarean birth was associated with more 'Don't know' responses in the exit survey concerning clinical interventions.
